defectsOutsideScope: Local Worker (wrangler/workerd) stalls after a request is refused before its body is read. Reproduced with a diagnostic script on this build, 25 rounds each: a refused PUT with a small body followed by a page request stalled 3 of 100 requests under Node 24 and 1 of 100 under Node 22 (8 s probe timeout); a refused 128 KiB body stalled 21 of 75 (Node 24) and 22 of 75 (Node 22); the control with no refused request had 0 of 25. One 503 was also seen. It makes the existing tests/worker-attendance-check.mjs stop after 257 checks on unmodified origin/main. This is a property of the local runtime or of refusing before reading the body (which TC-115 requires), not of the attendance change; it has not been tried on hosted Cloudflare. Any mounted procedure that sends a body-bearing request refused early is exposed to it.
The test catalogue needs an explicit line for every new mounted worker-*-check procedure, otherwise the guarded run refuses to start (exit 2). This is easy to miss and the brief does not mention it.
limits: Local Chromium on one machine, local D1 emulation, fictional synthetic data. Not cross-browser, not assistive-technology, not performance, not hosted.
The new triggers run in node:sqlite and the local Worker D1 emulation. They have not run on a hosted D1 database; the hosted deployment blocker from the handover is unchanged and untouched.
No designed case is accepted. 9 of 40 are blocked because they need reviewers, agreed policy or an environment that does not exist.
The legacy attendance POST can still overwrite without a reason (now logged, not prevented).
No school calendar exists, so there is no percentage, no school-day denominator and no term boundary. A session is class plus date.
Open policy decisions: calendar and terms, what an absence means, retention of the change log, family visibility of notes.
Real identity provider, ORF, paid AI and real-recipient delivery were not touched or enabled; there were 0 external requests in every mounted run.
